sections.h2: What is Gwinnett County like, and which cities does it include?
sections.html:
Gwinnett County is a core county of metro Atlanta, about nine miles northeast of the Atlanta city limits, with Lawrenceville as the seat and Peachtree Corners as its most populous city. Lawmakers established it on December 15, 1818, and the name comes from Button Gwinnett, who signed the Declaration of Independence (Wikipedia).

Total area is 437 square miles, of which 430 are land, across the upper Piedmont and along the Eastern Continental Divide. Lake Lanier reaches the extreme north, and part of the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area follows the northwest edge. Its northeastern corner was cut away in 1914 to help form Barrow County. Forsyth, Hall, Jackson, Barrow, Walton, Rockdale, DeKalb and Fulton counties share its borders.

Fifteen cities lie wholly or partly within the boundary: Auburn, Berkeley Lake, Buford, Dacula, Duluth, Grayson, Lawrenceville, Lilburn, Loganville, Mulberry, Norcross, Peachtree Corners, Snellville, Sugar Hill and Suwanee. Braselton and Rest Haven are towns, and Mountain Park is a census-designated place. Several of these cross into a neighboring county, so look at the parcel record to see which commissioner sends your bill.

sections.h2: Which roads, schools and employers shape a Gwinnett listing?
sections.html:
Interstate 85 and Interstate 985 are the main freeways, with US 23, US 29, US 78 and State Routes 8, 13 and 20 feeding them. Gwinnett County Airport, formerly Briscoe Field, is the county's own regional airfield, and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International is the closest major one. Workers average a 32.8-minute trip to work, which is worth mentioning to buyers.

The largest school system in the state is Gwinnett County Public Schools, running 143 schools: 21 high, 29 middle, 80 elementary and 13 specialty. Households within Buford city limits belong to the separate Buford City School District. Georgia Gwinnett College and Gwinnett Technical College are both in Lawrenceville.

Employers listed by Wikipedia include AGCO in Duluth, Comcast's Southeast headquarters and ASHRAE in Peachtree Corners, Canon's regional office in Norcross, and Primerica and Waffle House near Duluth and Norcross. Which district and city apply depends on where the parcel sits, and both should appear in your description of the property.

sections.h2: How large is Gwinnett County in the Census figures?
sections.html:
At the 2020 census the county held 957,062 people, second only to Fulton in Georgia. The July 2025 estimate stands at 1,018,099, up 6.3% from the estimates base, and housing units number 356,091. Foreign-born residents are 28.4% of the total. The county had 43,541 people in 1960 and 805,321 in 2010, a long climb that built the county's present digest.

sections.h2: Which Gwinnett County office handles which tax question?
sections.html:
Several offices share the work, and the tax commissioner's brochure names each. The commissioner sends bills and takes in and passes on the money, with no part in deciding the amount. The Board of Assessors sets values, while millage rates come from the commissioners, the school board and each city.

  • Property tax (tax commissioner): 770-822-8800, tax@gwinnettcounty.com, open weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Board of Assessors, real property: 770-822-7200; personal property: 770-822-7220. Values and appeals go through Gwinnett-Assessor.com.
  • Board of Commissioners, county millage rates and fees: 770-822-7000.
  • Board of Education, school millage: 678-301-6200.
  • Clerk of Court, deeds and liens: 770-822-8100.

The commissioner's brochure page is the best single reference, and its mailing address for payments is P.O. Box 372, Lawrenceville, GA 30046.

sections.h2: What does the Gwinnett County yearly tax calendar look like?
sections.html:
The county presents its dates as typical and subject to change, so the bill in your hand outranks any chart. The brochure sets out this order:

  • January: mobile home bills go out, with payment due April 1.
  • April 1: returns on business tangibles, aircraft and watercraft reach the Board of Assessors.
  • May and June: the Annual Notice of Assessment goes out, and appeals must be filed within 45 days of its date.
  • July and August: taxing bodies adopt millage rates through advertised, public processes.
  • August or September: real and personal property bills are mailed and also posted online.
  • October or November: payment comes due.

The page printed November 15, 2025 as the last due date and left the 2026 date to be determined, since the Board of Commissioners can change it yearly. Read your own bill for the date that applies. Personal property worth more than $20,000 combined is taxable, and a late or unreported return may draw a 10% penalty. A late mobile home bill adds a 10% penalty, then 1% interest each month after June 1.

sections.h2: What payment methods does Gwinnett County accept?
sections.html:
Paying online by check costs nothing, and online card payments add a convenience fee. Other options are the drop boxes open around the clock at all five tag offices, a mailed check to the Lawrenceville box, or a visit to any tax commissioner office. Cash must be handed over in person, and the county asks that none be mailed.

A few cities run their own property billing. The commissioner covers mobile home, heavy-duty equipment and timber tax in every city, yet real property inside a city that bills on its own is a question for that city's tax department.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply in Gwinnett County?
sections.html:
Homestead exemptions cut the tax on a primary residence, and a single application serves every exemption the county offers. It can be filed year-round by mail, at an office or online, provided you lived in the home as your legal primary residence on January 1. Approval continues until ownership or eligibility changes, and mailed forms should go by certified mail.

Gwinnett also has the Value Offset Exemption, a local measure that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of the bill. School and city taxes are not covered. It attaches automatically with a homestead approval and reaches the home plus as many as five acres of land. The Board of Assessors separately reviews conservation use, agricultural, historic and Brownfield preferential assessments and tax-exempt status for property such as places of worship.

sections.h2: What happens to Gwinnett County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Legal responsibility for the whole year rests with whoever owned on January 1. After a later sale, the earlier owner and the new owner both get a bill, and the commissioner takes no position on how they split it. That is for the two parties to settle, generally at the closing table.

An unpaid bill leads to a lien in the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows proof within 90 days of the due date that liability moved to the buyer. Acceptable proof pairs closing language in which the seller assigns property tax liability to the purchaser and the purchaser accepts it with a deed recorded in the purchaser's name. In the end a delinquent parcel can be sold at a tax auction.

faqs.q: When are Gwinnett County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Typically in October or November, following bills mailed in August or September. The county gave November 15, 2025 as the last due date and left 2026 to be determined, so rely on the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Gwinnett County value?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in May or June. The Board of Assessors takes the appeal, and the county says it can be filed online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if my Gwinnett County house sells after January 1?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner carries the full year, and both owners may receive a bill. Buyer and seller decide the split, usually on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What is the Gwinnett Value Offset Exemption?
faqs.a: A local exemption that holds assessed value at its base-year level for the county government share of your bill. School and city taxes are outside it, it reaches the home plus up to five acres, and it attaches automatically when a homestead exemption is granted.

faqs.q: Does Gwinnett County take cash for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but only face to face at a tax commissioner office. An online check payment is free and cards add a convenience fee. Never mail cash to the Lawrenceville box.
